entries.title: Exodus 22:2
segments:
Breaking up; breaking into a dwelling in the night. 
 
  No blood be shed; the man who killed him was not to be deemed guilty of murder, or be punished.

entries.title: Exodus 22:3
segments:
If the sun be risen; if it was in the daytime, the man could be seen and secured.  There was no need of killing him, and the wanton killing of him would be murder. 
 
  Be sold for his theft; that thus restitution may be made to the man from whom he has stolen.  Among the Jews, men were sometimes sold or bound out for a time, as a punishment for their crimes.  Their services were sold till they had made compensation to those whom they had injured.  A poor man sometimes sold his own services, or those of his children, or his creditors sold them for the payment of his debts.

entries.title: Exodus 22:5
segments: Restitution; a proper compensation to the person injured.

entries.title: Exodus 22:6
segments:
Make restitution; for the injury which his carelessness or neglect occasioned. 
 
When one man injures another through design or heedlessness, he is bound, as far as may be in his power, to make him suitable compensation.

entries.title: Exodus 22:7
segments: Stuff; furniture or articles of any kind.

entries.title: Exodus 22:8
segments: Put his hand; taken the article himself.

entries.title: Exodus 22:9
segments: Challengeth; affirms or declares.

entries.title: Exodus 22:10
segments: Fidelity in the safe preservation and good treatment of whatever is committed to us, is required by the law of God.  We should regard another's property as we ought to wish him to regard ours.

entries.title: Exodus 22:12
segments: Make restitution; on the ground of his not having taken proper care to prevent the theft.

entries.title: Exodus 22:13
segments: Bring it for witness; bring the animal, or some part of it, in proof of the fact.

entries.title: Exodus 22:14
segments: Make it good; presuming he had not taken proper care of it.

entries.title: Exodus 22:15
segments:
Not make it good; because the owner could see how it was treated. 
 
  It came for his hire; the price paid for the use of the beast was supposed to be enough not only to compensate for service, but also to cover the risk to which it would be exposed.  Of course, should the beast be hurt or die, the owner was to bear the loss. 
 
Whan a man hires property, giving a rent sufficient to compensate not only for its use, but also for the risk to which it is exposed, and the property without his fault is providentially injured or destroyed, the loss shall fall on the owner.

entries.title: Exodus 22:16
segments: Endow her; marry her, and suitably provide for her as his wife.

entries.title: Exodus 22:17
segments: According to the dowry; such as would be proper according to her rank and condition.

entries.title: Exodus 22:18
segments: A witch; one who professed to have conversed with evil spirits, and from them to receive supernatural power.

entries.title: Exodus 22:20
segments:
Shall be utterly destroyed; he not only broke the first commandment of the moral law, but also committed treason against the state, in acknowledging another God instead of Jehovah, who was then the civil head of the Jews. 
 
The restraints which are needful to keep men from outbreaking iniquity, show that their hearts are depraved; and tha all the holiness which there is among men is the fruit of divine grace.

entries.title: Exodus 22:21
segments: A stranger; one who came among them from another nation.

entries.title: Exodus 22:25
segments: Usury; interest.

entries.title: Exodus 22:27
segments: Strangers, widows, orphans, and poor persons are peculiarly exposed to be wronged by the wicked, and on this account God graciously makes them objects of his peculiar care, and with special severity will punish their oppressors.

entries.title: Exodus 22:28
segments: The gods; magistrates, judges, and other civil rulers, officers under God.

entries.title: Exodus 22:30
segments: Give it me; this was an acknowledgment of God as the rightful proprietor of all.

entries.title: Exodus 22:31
segments: Holy men unto me; separated from others to be peculiarly Jehovah's people.
